decisive_items: progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas involving the mandibular bodies, angles, ascending rami, and the maxillary tuberosities
response.rationale: Bilateral, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent areas is more consistent with Cherubism, a rare genetic disorder, than with other options.

rejected.why: Lack of abnormal hematologic tests makes Brown Tumor of Hyperparathyroidism less likely.
While radiographic findings are consistent with Central Giant Cell Granuloma, the bilateral and symmetrical nature of the swelling is more characteristic of Cherubism.
